basis: Five existing Week 6 objectives now have populated notes: four new answers and the unchanged placental-emergency response shared with Week 3. The three-bullet Quick answer / independently collapsed topics format is retained. Content follows the original Labor & Birth Complications PDF, with explicitly identified support from the supplied Pain Management and Postpartum Care PDFs. Limited safety/definition clarifications are labeled rather than attributed to the slides. Objective clauses unsupported in detail by the PDFs are explicitly identified; populated notes are not a claim that the original material supplies every protocol.

sharedObjective.handling: Unchanged complete object, including all original notes, metadata and sources. Reused in Week 6, Week 8 and the labor-emergencies topic. Its original source-page mapping and clarifications remain in docs/ob-week3-notes-audit.json.

visualReview.purpose: Reviewed original preview figures: episiotomy directions and laceration depths; cord presentations/prolapse, gravity-reducing positions and manual elevation; slide 35 timing language; supine McRoberts, suprapubic pressure and internal shoulder rotation. The all-fours knee-chest illustration is not misidentified as McRoberts. No complete clinical case history is inferred from diagrams.

Verified the limited inversion definition/list and absence of a replacement protocol; reviewed brief post-cesarean bowel and lochia/incision assessment material. These pages do not supply a complete operative-birth recovery or discharge pathway.

clarifications.issue: Preterm boundary written <37 6/7; steroid benefit/timing shorthand; magnesium listed as PPROM labor suppression
clarifications.handling: Uses <37 completed weeks; explains corticosteroid maturation versus selected short-term tocolysis versus magnesium neuroprotection. No replacement dose schedule or expanded gestational eligibility table.

clarifications.issue: Routine bed rest/activity restrictions and one-hour home symptom trial
clarifications.handling: Symptoms/leakage prompt contact rather than delayed evaluation; routine restriction is not presented as prevention treatment.

clarifications.issue: Fetal fibronectin suggested when ROM suspected
clarifications.handling: Distinguishes selected preterm-birth risk assessment with intact membranes from confirmation of membrane rupture.

clarifications.issue: PROM defined by one-hour interval; PPROM induction/antibiotics framed as automatic 24-hour/34-week rules
clarifications.handling: Defines prelabor rupture without a required interval, PPROM <37 weeks, individualized gestation/status-based planning and prompt response to infection/compromise.

clarifications.issue: Abbreviated operative vaginal eligibility and three pop-offs phrased as a continuation allowance
clarifications.handling: Clarifies full dilation/membranes/head position/analgesia and backup readiness; poor progress or compromise requires reassessment before a numeric limit is reached.

clarifications.issue: Anesthetic-space, fixed-preload and dilation shorthand in supportive pain PDF
clarifications.handling: Separates epidural/intrathecal anatomy and follows an individualized anesthesia plan rather than importing the fixed rules.

clarifications.issue: Two-minute shoulder-dystocia waiting rule; ambiguous McRoberts wording; ordinary cesarean escalation after head birth
clarifications.handling: Immediate recognition/help, correct supine hyperflexed positioning, no fundal/excessive traction, immediate expert rescue rather than an ordinary transfer, and concise timing/documentation/newborn follow-up clarification.

clarifications.issue: Cord manipulation/decompression and routine maternal oxygen listed for fetal distress
clarifications.handling: Maintain elevation of presenting part, minimize cord handling/do not replace cord above fetus, prioritize birth and use oxygen for maternal hypoxia/clinical indication rather than routinely for normoxic FHR changes.

clarifications.issue: Rupture/AFE slides mainly list findings; AFE implies fetal cells confirm the diagnosis and quotes older mortality estimates
clarifications.handling: Labels immediate response priorities, distinguishes AFE as a clinical diagnosis, and omits unneeded older mortality claims, resuscitation doses and surgical details.

clarifications.issue: Inversion appears near general atony/fundal-massage material without specific response
clarifications.handling: Labels urgent specialist replacement/resuscitation, distinguishes inversion from routine atony massage and uterotonic use, and marks the absence of a complete source protocol.

materialLimits.handling: The slides support recognition, medication purposes and broad care priorities but not a complete gestation-specific PROM/PTL algorithm, dystocia treatment protocol or universal labor-arrest thresholds. Notes mark this limit and avoid filling it with new tables or protocols.

The original Week 6 deck has brief operative-vaginal/VBAC/cesarean indications, not a complete cesarean nursing pathway. Supplied pain/postpartum PDFs contribute consent, anesthesia and recovery assessments. A full preoperative checklist, timed postoperative regimen, first-walk time, feeding progression and specific home restrictions remain explicitly unsupplied.

The original PDFs have recognition lists and cord diagrams, not full case histories or comprehensive rupture/AFE/inversion protocols. Inversion’s definition comes from the supplied postpartum PDF; only essential safety response is clarified externally. No fictional cases or new surgical/resuscitation regimen is authored.

sharedViews: The four new answers appear in Week 6 and the existing Week 8 review; shoulder dystocia and the other emergencies also populate the existing labor-emergencies topic. The shared placental-emergency object, all earlier notes, weekly/topic mappings, main exam-topic order, original PDFs/previews, infographic/presentation layout, videos, practice and navigation are unchanged.
limits: Source-led educational summaries with identified source gaps. Automated checks verify mapped coverage, original-source integrity, preserved prior answers and shared safe rendering; they are not independent clinical validation or a new mobile-browser usability test.
